core_obligations: Establish the properties (proof lines 6243-6251): by the companion results of the same chapter, a universally injective integral morphism has properties (A), (B) and (C), and the associated base change functor is almost cocontinuous.

Derive the first three clauses (proof lines 6251-6260): property (C) gives reflection of injections and surjections, almost cocontinuity gives commutation with finite connected colimits, and property (B) gives that surjections are transformed into surjections.

Derive the remaining clauses (proof lines 6260-6266): clauses (4), (5) and (6) follow formally from the first three by the general exactness results for morphisms of sites, and clause (7) is the almost cocontinuity already established.
proof_roadmap: Use the companion results to get properties (A), (B), (C) and almost cocontinuity.
Read off the first three clauses from those properties through the corresponding implications.
Deduce the exactness and faithfulness clauses formally, and record the last clause.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects seven consequences of the assumption that a morphism of schemes is universally injective and integral (statement lines 6204-6241, a statement with seven numbered clauses). The proof is a complete chain of named inputs: the companion results of the same chapter give properties (A), (B) and (C) together with almost cocontinuity of the base change functor (proof lines 6243-6251); the implications from those properties give the first three clauses (proof lines 6251-6260); and the remaining clauses, concerning surjectivity of the unit, faithfulness and exactness, follow formally through the general exactness results for morphisms of sites (proof lines 6260-6266). The non-formal content is the assembly of the seven clauses out of these inputs, each of which the author names. The claim is H2: one structured reduction, every step attributed.
